  "text": "The water ran hard for a minute, carrying sand and bits of weed out toward the harbor. Then it slowed to a steady stream. Mr. Venn crouched beside the opening and held his lantern close, though the afternoon was still bright.

“There’s daylight at the other end,” he said.

The harbor master sent one of the men up to the sluice gate. Mara watched him turn the wheel. Deep inside the wall, something creaked. Water that had been pooling behind the quay began to drain, first in narrow threads, then in a broad, muddy current.

Mrs. Bell poured tea into the flask’s tin cups. Daniel took one to their father, who had not moved from Mara’s side.

“Will it keep the cottages dry?” Daniel asked.

“It should help,” their father said. “We’ll know more after the next high tide.”

The harbor master had already taken out his notebook. He wrote down the condition of the grating and asked Mr. Venn to arrange a proper inspection in the morning. He also asked where the drawing had been found.

“In the books by our hearth,” Mara said.

He looked up, surprised, and she explained about the rain coming through the cottage roof. Daniel added that the books were drying now, though a few pages had stuck together.

“Well,” the harbor master said, closing his notebook, “take care of them. There may be other plans we’ve forgotten.”

On the walk home, the rain stopped. Daniel ran ahead to check the books, while Mara and her father followed slowly. At the cottage, a thin strip of sunlight lay across the hearth."
